subject: tiny ants
title: These Ants Build a Trap Full of Holes, Then Stretch Prey Out on It

scenes.text: These ants build a trap. It works like a torture rack.
They live on one Amazon plant, and build a gallery from its hairs, pierced with dozens of holes.
They reinforce it with a fungus they spread themselves.
Then a worker waits under every hole, jaws wide open.
An insect lands. Ants seize its legs and antennae and pull, pinning it flat, while others swarm in to sting.
The prey can be far bigger than any ant. Scientists called them the first ants known to build a trap.

description:
A tiny Amazon ant, Allomerus decemarticulatus, builds a trap along the stems of its host plant, Hirtella physophora, in French Guiana.
The ants make a gallery from the plant's hairs, reinforce it with a fungus and leave it full of holes. Workers wait in the holes with jaws open, grab the legs and antennae of any insect that lands, stretch it out and hold it while others sting. The researchers who described it in Nature in 2005 said it was the first time ants had been seen building a trap to ambush prey.
Which animal builds the nastiest trap? Comment below.
first_comment: The queen carries the fungus from plant to plant when she founds a new colony. Trap-building ants or web-building spiders: which is smarter?
